stops.stop: Zurich, the brain-anatomy laboratory
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction. The laboratory is Constantin von Monakow's brain-anatomy institute, which was in ZURICH, not Vienna: Monakow directed it there from the 1880s until his death in 1930. English Wikipedia names the institute in connection with The Sensory Order but does not place it, and an earlier draft of this file wrongly attached it to the University of Vienna. The visit followed the fuel-shortage closure of the University of Vienna and is placed in 1920; the year is not independently confirmed against a primary record, and the month is an ordering device only.

stops.stop: London School of Economics, the review and Sraffa's answer
stops.date_confidence: attested and corrected here. Hayek's review of Keynes's Treatise on Money ran in Economica in two parts, August 1931 and February 1932. Piero Sraffa's 'Dr. Hayek on Money and Capital' appeared in the Economic Journal in 1932 (42: 42-53), with a rejoinder in June 1932, and its target was Prices and Production rather than the Treatise review. An earlier draft compressed the whole exchange into 1931; it spans 1931-1932. Keynes's 'frightful muddle' remark is widely quoted and was not re-verified against a primary Keynes text in this pass.
